name: Rekab
title: Ancestor of the Rechabites
summary: Rekab is best known as the father of Jonadab (also called Jehonadab), who established the rules for living followed by the Rechabites. The Rechabites were known for their strict lifestyle: they did not drink wine, build houses, sow grain, or plant vineyards, but lived in tents. Their faithfulness to these commands was used by the prophet Jeremiah as an example of obedience to God.

keyEvents.title: Rekab as ancestor of the Rechabites
keyEvents.description: Rekab is mentioned as the forefather of the clan known as the Rechabites, a group that lived according to strict ascetic rules.

keyEvents.title: Jonadab's alliance with Jehu
keyEvents.description: Rekab's son Jonadab (Jehonadab) joined King Jehu in his fight against Baal worship in Israel, demonstrating the clan's zeal for the Lord.

keyEvents.title: The Rechabites' rules for living
keyEvents.description: The prophet Jeremiah describes the strict rules for living that Jonadab, Rekab's son, imposed on his descendants: to abstain from wine, not build houses, and live in tents.

keyEvents.title: Jeremiah Tests the Rechabites
keyEvents.description: God asked Jeremiah to invite the Rechabites to the temple and offer them wine. They refused to drink, demonstrating their loyalty to Jonadab's command.

keyEvents.title: The Rechabites' Obedience as an Example
keyEvents.description: God used the Rechabites' obedience to their ancestor's command as a contrast to Judah's disobedience to the Lord's word. Their faithfulness was held up as an example.

keyEvents.title: God's Blessing on the Rechabites
keyEvents.description: Because of their loyalty, God promised that there would always be a descendant of Jonadab son of Rekab standing before the Lord.
